- **self**: Interest rate curves utilization and borrow-supply APY formulas (3/2)

## Structure and components

- [statement] In klend, utilization = borrowed / total_supply, where total_supply = available + borrowed - accumulated protocol fees - accumulated referrer fees - pending referrer fees. Borrowers pay the curve rate plus the reserve's host_fixed_interest_rate_bps. In compound_interest, the interest on the host rate goes entirely to accumulated protocol fees. The protocol take rate applies only to the variable part, and referrer fees come out of the protocol's take, so lenders keep variable interest x (1 - protocol_take_rate_pct / 100). The SDK's calculateSupplyAPR returns utilization x borrow rate x (1 - take rate) and excludes reserve rewards. Kamino's safeguards page writes the same rule as S = U x B x (1 - R). (high confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kamino-Finance/klend/master/programs/klend/src/state/reserve.rs · keywords: Interest rate curves utilization and borrow-supply APY formulas · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kamino-Finance/klend-sdk/master/src/classes/reserve.ts, https://kamino.com/docs/risk/safeguards/interest-rates

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The purpose of the steep upper leg is to keep utilization off 100%: at 100% all deposits are lent out and lenders cannot withdraw until borrowers repay or new supply arrives. Kamino says this causes no loss of funds but is the highest-lender-rate state. The marginfi README says high interest at 90%+ utilization pushes borrowers to repay and describes optimal utilization as typically 80-90%. (medium confidence) — https://kamino.com/docs/risk/safeguards/interest-rates · keywords: Interest rate curves utilization and borrow-supply APY formulas · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrgnlabs/marginfi-v2/main/README.md
- [statement] The kinked curve exists to keep utilization away from 100%, where every deposit is lent out and lenders cannot withdraw. Kamino says its model makes 100% utilization economically unsustainable and that 100% causes no loss of funds but blocks withdrawals. The marginfi README says high interest at 90%+ utilization pushes borrowers to repay. Velocity argues a single straight line cannot do both jobs: tuned to 50% at 100% it charges 40% at 80%, and tuned to 10% at 80% it charges only 12.5% at 100%, so a kink with steep upper segments is needed. (high confidence) — https://kamino.com/docs/risk/safeguards/interest-rates · keywords: Interest rate curves utilization and borrow-supply APY formulas · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrgnlabs/marginfi-v2/main/README.md, https://docs.velocity.exchange/lend-borrow/borrow-interest-rate
